context: This authored note demonstrates research communication.
It reports no experiment, score or model outcome.

changes.title: Name the baseline
before: This note compares the candidate result.
after: This note compares the candidate result with a named baseline.
changes.why: The previous sentence names a candidate but leaves the alternative unstated. The revision makes the comparison explicit before a reader interprets a difference.
changes.protects: A result should identify what it is being compared with.

changes.title: Attach the denominator
before: The aggregate is reported as a percentage.
after: The aggregate includes the numerator, denominator and unit.
The evaluation cohort is named alongside the measurement.
changes.why: A percentage alone hides the amount and kind of evidence. The revision requires the count, unit and cohort to travel with the reported value.
changes.protects: The reader can distinguish questions, examples and runs.

changes.title: Qualify the estimate
before: A higher point estimate establishes improvement.
after: The point estimate is read alongside its uncertainty interval.
The interval method and its scope are recorded.
changes.why: The original wording turns a point estimate into an unsupported conclusion. The revision asks for uncertainty context before interpreting the estimate. No actual estimate or interval is supplied in this fixture.
changes.protects: A stronger-sounding sentence must not outrun its evidence.

changes.title: Keep scope and provenance
before: The finding generalizes beyond this evaluation.
after: The finding is limited to this study and its recorded conditions.
Source: authored example record; no measured outcome is reported.
changes.why: The previous sentence asserts generalization without supporting evidence. The revised wording carries the boundary and source identity beside the finding, and states that this document is illustrative.
changes.protects: A qualification and source remain attached to the conclusion.
